description: How each Marketing Engineer run works around the agent: its task definition, weekly schedule, the agent's time limit, how its work is counted for the run report, the 14-day window, whether the Waitlist is live, the size of a Beta Cohort invitation batch, the outputs and sources its run report accounts for, the records step that saves workspace/ and ledger/ to main, and the prices behind its approximate cost. The launcher reads this file; the agent cannot write it (G8). The exchange with Mandu: docs/mandu-exchange.md. Operating the production clone: docs/operations.md.

schedule.why: The Founder's Mandu sitting is Sunday evening. 16:00 in the Mac's local time zone leaves a few hours to finish, or to re-run on demand, before it.

agent.why: Every run must end with its report (US-ME17), so the launcher stops an agent still running this many seconds after it started, with every process the Mac's process table shows it started, and finishes the run as timed out. The seconds are wall-clock time from the agent's start, the Mac's sleep included: nothing keeps the Mac awake for a run and a sleeping Mac runs nothing, so the stop of an agent the Mac slept past the limit starts within about a second of the Mac waking, and the run report says about how long the Mac slept. Awake time is counted too, and the agent is stopped at whichever count reaches the limit first, so a wall clock set back cannot extend a run; one set forward can end it early. Basis: the limit was set while the agent ran at Codex's default medium reasoning effort, when the 46 weekly runs with the real agent that ran to their end on the Founder's Mac between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-11 took 18 to 218 seconds from the run's start to the agent's end, median 49, 35 of them under 90, and 1800 seconds, 30 minutes, was about 8 times the longest. Since 2026-10-11 the agent runs at high effort (codex.reasoning_effort in config/guardrails/runtime.json) and takes longer. The ten runs measured on that change, each a package review and the first batch's seven post Drafts, took 283 to 1,122 seconds of agent time, median 646, nine of them with four or five such sessions running at once on the Mac and one, at 428 seconds, with none of its own beside it; the investigation before the change measured 271 to 897 seconds. The limit is left at 1800 seconds. It is now about 1.6 times the longest run measured and 2.8 times the median, not 8 times: every run measured ended inside it, the longest at 62 percent of it, but a session that also carries the workflows still to be built, or runs on a busy Mac, can come near it, and the run report's Agent time line shows each run's time against it. A run that starts at 16:00 on a Mac that stays awake and is cut at the limit still ends hours before the Sunday evening sitting; on a Mac that sleeps past the limit, the run ends when the Mac wakes. There is no separate, shorter limit on silence: Codex's event stream reports only whole steps, with no sign of progress inside one. The longest run went 35 seconds without an event while it worked, and nothing bounds a step but the work in it, so a long step and a stalled model stream look the same from outside. Raise the limit here, through a reviewed change, if run reports show healthy runs coming near it; it must be above zero and at most 86400, a day.

work_counts.source: Measured on 2026-10-11 with Codex CLI 0.160.0 and gpt-6-luna, started with the launcher's own Codex command: of one command's 180,000 characters of output, Codex showed the model the first 20,000 and the last 20,000, with a note that 35,003 of 45,003 tokens were cut. That is the model catalog's truncation policy for this model, 10,000 tokens, at the 4 characters Codex counts to a token.
work_counts.why: The run report shows what the launcher counted of the agent's session beside the agent's own Review line (US-ME17), because that line is the agent's word and has read complete after the shallowest sessions. One count is how many of the package files the brief listed the agent read. Codex's event stream holds every command's whole output, whatever the model was shown of it, and a session that prints all the package files in one command is shown only the first and last of them. So the launcher counts a file as read only when at least half of its lines of 24 characters or more came back in the part of some command's output that Codex shows the model: the whole output up to this many characters, else its first and last halves of this many. A file with no line that long is counted only when a command that names its path was shown its whole text, since its short lines are in any output. The launcher sets no output limit of its own. This figure describes Codex, so measure it again and change it here, through a reviewed change, after a Codex upgrade or a change of model. The counts inform the Founder and gate nothing.

window.why: Day 1 of the 14-day window follows from the Founder's sitting: first_sitting is the date (YYYY-MM-DD, on the schedule's day) of the sitting that approves the window's first batch, day 1 is the day after it, and every calendar day follows from day 1. Which sitting that is, and the window's one fixed evening posting slot (HH:MM, the Mac's local time), are the Founder's call (FR-8), set here through a reviewed change and never inferred, since nothing posts before the Waitlist is live; the kit's posting-slot rule in the calendar names no time, so the time is set here. Until first_sitting is set, every run prepares calendar days 1 to 7 as the first batch, with no slot; once it is set, each run prepares the calendar days that fall in the week after the coming sitting, and a post's slot is its date at this time once slot is set too.

waitlist.why: No public post may go out before the Waitlist is live (FR-9). live_since is the date (YYYY-MM-DD) the Waitlist went live, set here through a reviewed change once US-ME05's Validation Test has passed on reptoday.app, and never inferred from whether a source is connected or what it is named. While it is null, or a date still ahead, every post item, the run brief, and the run report say that nothing can be published until the Waitlist is live.

beta_recruiting.why: How many Waitlist entries one Beta Cohort invitation batch offers the Founder (US-ME15), the Founder's call, changed here through a reviewed change. The Founder confirmed capped batches and chose 20 on 2026-10-11. At most one batch is open at a time, and the next is offered only after the Founder has decided the last, so a week's sends and first sessions stay manageable. It cannot be larger than the cohort's maximum in config/products.json.

records.why: Only the production clone syncs and saves records; every other checkout runs without touching git. Setting sync_before_run or save_after_run to false turns that step off.

cost.why: The run report states the run's approximate cost at API prices from Codex's token counts.
